title: HikariCP Connection Pool Exhaustion under Flash Sale Concurrency
symptoms: 504 Gateway Timeout on POST /api/v1/charge, spikes in active DB pool connection metrics (100% capacity), HTTP 500 error rate > 45%.
rootCause: HikariCP connection pool max size was capped at 20 default connections. Under high concurrent checkout requests, database connections were held during external Stripe API calls without timeouts, starving pool threads.
runbookExecuted: RB-PAY-04: Emergency connection pool scale & socket timeout patch
resolutionSteps: Bumped HikariCP maximumPoolSize from 20 to 150 via Helm environment config.
Applied 3000ms read timeout on downstream Stripe HTTP client calls to release pooled connections quickly.
Flushed transient deadlock keys in Redis cluster.
learnedBestPractice: Never perform synchronous external HTTP calls while holding an open database transaction lock. Set explicit HTTP client connection & read timeouts.

title: Node.js Heap Memory Leak in RS256 JWT Key Cache
symptoms: auth-service pod restart loop (OOMKilled exit code 137), RSS memory growing linearly by 85MB/min under high auth token verification volume.
rootCause: JWKS key cache map in Auth0 verification middleware used un-capped key string keys without TTL eviction, causing heap accumulation on every token refresh.
runbookExecuted: RB-AUTH-09: Hot-reload LRU cache patch & rolling restart
resolutionSteps: Replaced standard JavaScript Object key cache with quick-lru capped at 1000 entries.
Issued rolling restart across auth-service deployment (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service`).
Increased container memory limits from 512Mi to 1Gi as temporary buffer.
learnedBestPractice: All in-memory caches in microservices MUST have strict size bounds and TTL eviction to prevent RSS memory leak OOMKilled crashes.

title: Redis Cache Stampede & Thundering Herd on Product Catalog Key
symptoms: Database CPU utilization spiked to 99%, microservice latency degraded from 12ms to 4800ms following scheduled cache key expiration.
rootCause: Hot cache key 'cat:homepage:v2' expired at top of the hour. 5,000 concurrent client threads simultaneously missed cache and hammered primary PostgreSQL DB instance.
runbookExecuted: RB-REDIS-02: Mutex lock caching & probabilistic early expiration
resolutionSteps: Enabled single-flight / mutex lock pattern on catalog service cache miss fallback.
Re-populated hot cache key manually using redis-cli with background worker script.
Implemented randomized jitter (±300s) on key expiration TTLs.
learnedBestPractice: Prevent thundering herd by using single-flight request coalescing for DB queries and applying TTL jitter to popular cache keys.

title: Autovacuum Lock Contention & Transaction ID Mappings Spike
symptoms: PostgreSQL Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) disk space 92% full, transaction ID wraparound warning alerts, blocking locks on user_sessions table.
rootCause: Long-running analytics query in background reporting worker held open transaction snapshot for over 6 hours, preventing autovacuum from cleaning dead tuples.
runbookExecuted: RB-DB-07: Cancel idle transactions & trigger targeted vacuum analyze
resolutionSteps: Terminated blocking analytics query PID using `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid)`.
Configured `statement_timeout = 30s` on default analytics reporting role.
learnedBestPractice: Always enforce statement_timeout on non-OLTP analytical database connections to prevent autovacuum freeze and transaction ID wraparound.

title: Stripe Webhook Signature Verification Failures due to Proxy Header Truncation
symptoms: Payment status stuck in 'PENDING', 400 Bad Request responses on incoming webhook notifications from Stripe endpoint.
rootCause: NGINX ingress controller header buffer size (4k) truncated long `Stripe-Signature` headers during TLS cipher renegotiation.
runbookExecuted: RB-PAY-12: Ingress buffer size override & webhook retry trigger
resolutionSteps: Triggered Stripe API event resend CLI command to replay missed webhook payloads.
learnedBestPractice: Configure ingress proxy buffer sizes to at least 16k when receiving cryptographically signed webhook headers from third-party APIs.
